I think the first thing I'd say is we're really proud of the cash generation we've been able to deliver on since the merger that it ultimately is resulting in our -- in a position that we're in to have more flexibility as it relates to capital deployment. And with net leverage now at 2.7x and obviously, the share repurchase authorization that we announced yesterday evening, we're in a position to have greater flexibility in how we allocate excess capital.

Obviously, we've signaled that our current valuation provides an attractive opportunity to invest in our own business while maintaining flexibility to fund organic growth, pursue strategic acquisitions, which is at the heart of your question, and also preserve a prudent balance sheet. We've also signaled that we expect net leverage below 2.5x. So I think that just shows our commitment to make sure we're maintaining that optionality and flexibility moving forward. And as it relates to M&A, obviously, we've said that we're going to focus on the capital deployment opportunities that provide the highest risk-adjusted rate of return.

So you'll think about our M&A as being capability focused and it's going to have to meet very high strategic and financial criteria to ensure that we adhere to that commitment.

John E. Heller: And I think trust is really important. And when we set out over 2 years ago, we said our focus was on getting leverage below 3x and we focused on that as a leadership team, focusing on integration, organic growth and cash flow. And we're now excited about being at 2.7 leverage and continuing to focus on delevering and now with the opportunity to have a share repurchase program. But at the same time, we'll look to invest in our business. But we're going to focus on investments in those higher-margin accretive end markets that we've discussed around Digital Solutions, cyber, space and nuclear that we think have great tailwinds, generational tailwinds that can help drive our business forward.

But as Travis said, we're going to be very judicious in how we deploy cash in a way that can drive the best shareholder value.

Tobey Sommer: If I may ask a follow-up in your guidance for '27, do you -- is there any difference in the rate of growth between your domestic business and your international exposure? And if so, kind of which one is leading the way?

Travis Barton Johnson: There's no material difference between the domestic and international growth in the '27 guide.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Andre Madrid with U.S. Bancorp BTIG.

Andre Madrid: I wanted to start first on maybe FY '27 outlook at a segment level. How should we be thinking about growth and EBITDA expectations through the year looking at the 2 segments?

Travis Barton Johnson: So it's interesting as you look at it at a segment level. Obviously, this year, Digital Solutions had a remarkable year from an organic growth perspective, delivering 8% growth in the fourth quarter, 7% for the year. Obviously, the NASA insourcing will impact the growth trajectory of that segment next year. So you can think about it being down low to mid-single digits as a result of that NASA headwind.

At the same time, we saw margins stabilize in that segment in the back half of the year, and that's going to provide a good launch point for them as we head into FY '27, and I think they'll be the predominant driver of the margin expansion that we expect in the year. And then on Global Engineering Solutions, obviously, a little bit of an opposite story there. Growth was a little bit more pressured in FY '26, but we've had some really nice wins in that segment that are going to drive the growth in FY '27 with NITE, the U.S. Army work we're doing in Germany, just to name a few things. And then we'll expect their margins.

They had 100 basis points margin expansion in FY '26. So we'll expect that to be consistent as we head into FY '27.

Andre Madrid: Got it. That's really helpful. And then maybe just looking ahead of '27, I'm not trying to piece out what your what you guys are anticipating. But you have provided the 4% to 6% long-term growth outlook previously even excluding the NASA impact this year, you're kind of at the low end of the range. I'm really just trying to understand what gets you -- what would need to happen to see the midpoint or even the high end of your long-term growth outlook? And maybe even beyond that, like what's the bull case here that you guys foresee that would get you to, I guess, at the midpoint or the higher end of your range?

Travis Barton Johnson: Yes, I'll offer a few thoughts, and John might add as well. I think you're exactly right in thinking about exactly how we're thinking about it. First, the underlying business is going to grow 4% this year, excluding the impact of NASA. So that's a good launch point as we head into FY '28 and beyond. Second, I think you got to look at the leading indicators in our business development performance that we've seen since the merger, 1.2x in FY '25, 1.2x in FY '26, excluding the NASA debooking that we saw. So the business development engine is working. We continue to see strong demand for our solutions that we offer to our customers.

We continue to see a high volume. We exceeded our $35 billion submits target this year, as John noted in his prepared remarks, and as I said earlier, we're ending the year in $25 billion of pending awards. So we think that the foundation for that mid-single-digit growth continues to be there, and kind of the history there, excluding the headwinds, which we don't expect things like NASA to continue into the future, give us a good confidence in how growth will look '28 and beyond.

John E. Heller: I also think it's our end market focus. We've talked a lot about space that we are in a very solid position in terms of the work we do across NASA, Missile Defense Agency, Space Force and the growing demand for services and technology that's going to drive that market forward and where we sit right in the epicenter of all that. Our work in cyber, which we continue to see the challenge and the opportunity that exists in the cyber area across every end market that we support, every customer. And then of course, nuclear in general, that this is a market that is starting to expand with many different projects in the works.

As these projects come online, our revenue profile increases and it's going to take time for some of these projects to matriculate and you think of the SMR areas, we are working with a large number of OEMs in helping bring SMR technology to certification level so that they can begin construction. Once these designs get approved and these projects move into production, that will mean a significant uptick. And we put out a profile, and it's in today's presentation that shows '26 to '30, '30 to '35, the growth we expect in the nuclear market.

And we're still confident we had showed this to everyone in the past, and we wanted to reiterate that based on the confidence we're seeing in the nuclear market in general. And we expect to see that be a key driver of growth '28 and beyond.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Greg Parrish with Morgan Stanley.

Gregory (Greg) Parrish: Congrats on the quarter. Maybe just starting with the 4% normalized top line guidance. I mean, how would you characterize the level of conservatism built in? Is there room to outperform some of the newly awarded contracts that are built in? Is there risk from any protest there? Just maybe help us with the line of sight.

Travis Barton Johnson: Sure. I would say, just like any year, we provide a range that provides a variety of different potential outcomes. That said, I think it's a reasonable guide. And I also say, just repeat what I said earlier in the fact that we've got better visibility this year at this time than we had last year, right? So we still have 6% of new business to achieve, but we've got a good line of sight into that. Nice start to the year here in the first quarter, but still have work to do. But coming from a position of strength with 94% in firm or recompete is certainly a good place to start the year.

And then also having a few contracts which are already in transition. We're not dependent on protest resolution on them. They were already protested once, and now they're out of protest, and we've actually begun work on them in the first quarter here. NITE is a good example of that. U.S. Army work we're doing in Germany, another good example of that.

John E. Heller: Yes. And I think if you look at the market environment, too, I think it's important to understand that we're seeing pretty good stable bid volume. We're -- of course, protests are normal and occur in just about every instance. So we factor that in, but we're pretty satisfied with the bid volume. Awards are slower. It just take -- still take some time. I think there are -- what you would say, our customers are faced with a number of priorities like war in the Middle East and that -- and the administration changes in policy and other things. But we've seen these in the past.

And although we haven't seen necessarily an opportunity to see some of these factors disappear. We have tried to reflect that in our guidance going forward.

Gregory (Greg) Parrish: Yes, fair enough. That's all very helpful. And then maybe just one on the defense budget. How do you view the Senate version? I'm not sure if there's anything to call out there. And then what are your big items that you're watching for in the final bill?

John E. Heller: Well, we fully expect that there will be bipartisan support for defense spending. So I think everyone is kind of expecting that somewhere between $1 trillion and $1.1 trillion. But frankly, we're not counting on anything specific in the budget itself, as long as we're in that range, I mean, let's face it, this is still significantly higher than we have seen in prior years. So from our perspective, it remains -- the outlook still remains positive. Also keep in mind that 20% of our revenue is derived from other than U.S. government sources and those end markets, international, AUKUS in Australia, where we have seen recent success and very excited about the future there.

The U.K. both on the defense and nuclear infrastructure side and then overall nuclear energy itself driving demand for our business. So we feel pretty comfortable about the U.S. budget expectations, along with the non-U.S. sources of revenue remaining strong and supportive of our plan for '27.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Trevor Walsh with Citizens JMP.

Trevor Walsh: Travis, you touched on it a little bit in one of the prior answers to a couple of questions ago. But you mentioned the $35 billion in submit bid volume kind of target made for '26. Are you able to provide or maybe even just at a high level, give us a sense of what the magnitude of that is going to be in '27 as far as expected bids and how that's factoring or not into guidance?

John E. Heller: Yes. And we talked about a very strong year in '26, probably above our expectations in some respects, and that was great. Some of those might have been a little bit earlier than we expected, which drove the number up. But we're still expecting for '27 around $35 billion, and hopefully, we set that kind of expectation with our team. Our team does a great job of identifying work and trying to exceed expectations. So at a minimum, we're confident in our pipeline that we can hit that $35 billion submit target again.

Travis Barton Johnson: The other thing that I'd add is we're focused on quality, not just quantity, and making sure that we're pursuing the opportunities where we have the highest right to win, and our capabilities are best aligned with what the requirements of the customer are. So it's -- volume can ebb and flow depending on what's out there, but we're just as much focused on the quality of the opportunity. And the second thing I would say as it relates to '27, we're not counting on a significant volume of submit award translate to revenue in the fiscal year '27. So really, what we're going to be submitting in '27 will have an impact in '28 and beyond.

Trevor Walsh: Got it. Super helpful. Appreciate it both. Maybe just a quick follow-up, more on just some cash flow dynamics. Anything to call out as far as seasonality in '27? I appreciate the build you provided for cash flow for the full year, over $600 million. Anything quarterly we should think about that's maybe different this year? And then just generally speaking, I know you're not going beyond '27, but as we think about maybe those tax payments that seem to be kind of coming in a little bit, is that about what we should expect, Travis, kind of in the year-to-year just range or I guess, just size of that going forward now?

Or just trying to get a little bit more how we don't want to get over our skis as far as free cash flow in and out years.

Travis Barton Johnson: Yes, sure. We're really happy with how we ended the year from a free cash flow perspective, came in a little bit above our expectations due to some working capital timing as well as lower cash tax payments we were able to realize from some tax planning initiatives. So really nice place to end the year coming in above the high end of our guidance range there. Obviously, like I said, there could be some timing associated with that. But looking to FY '27, we're confident in our ability to deliver greater than $600 million. And from a time phasing perspective, you may recall in '26, there was a bit of a difference in the number of pay periods.

That will be consistent from '26 to '27. So you can expect the cadence to be relatively consistent with what you saw in FY '26. The only thing I would call out that might be a little different is we did have the impact of the government shutdown in Q1 of last year, which was roughly $100 million and then that recovered in the second quarter of '26. So we'll expect that to be a little bit more normalized in '27. But other than that, the cadence will remain pretty consistent with Q1 being an outflow quarter, call it, $75 million to $100 million and Q4 being the strongest quarter.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Ronald Epstein with Bank of America.

Andrew Steinhardt: This is Andrew Steinhardt on for Ron. I guess, just first here, how are you guys thinking about the potential impacts of an extended CR into calendar 2027? Is that scenario a threat to any existing work in the portfolio or more so an impact to potential awards on new programs?

John E. Heller: Yes. I mean we've been through this, I don't know, just about every year. And we have seen minimal impact in the past, and we expect the same thing. Our work is very tied to critical mission support. And of course, 20% of our work is not U.S. government as well. So of the U.S. government work, we have traditionally seen minimal impact from CR given the work we're doing is funded long-term contracts, average contract length, 7 to 8 years and tied to basic critical missions that have to get done for the government to operate. So just we're expecting minimal to no impact.

Andrew Steinhardt: Got it. Got it. Makes sense. And just a quick follow-up. I guess, just in terms of the capital allocation strategy with the $500 million authorized for buybacks. Where do your guys' priorities stand beyond share buybacks?

Travis Barton Johnson: Yes. So a few thoughts there. First, I think we wanted to be transparent on where we were focused in the near term, given the opportunity that we think the current valuation presents -- the opportunity that the current valuation presents. So we provided that we're targeting to deploy 50% in FY '27 of the $500 million share repurchase authorization. At the same time, we're focused on maintaining a prudent balance sheet and signaled that we intend to end the year with net leverage less than 2.5x.

And then looking at M&A still from a capability, strategic focus is still going to be on the road map, but as we talked about earlier, it's going to have to be aligned with clear strategic and financial criteria to move that forward. So that's how we're thinking about it here in the near term.

John E. Heller: I think we've outlined our strategy this past year, our focus on key national security end markets and nuclear. I outlined some of those again on this call. We think we're having great progress in areas like space and cyber and nuclear and digital. And frankly, we think the market undervalues Amentum. And we're confident of the strength of this company and the value of this company. And as the market undervalues it, we see it as an opportunity given our strong free cash flow. And so that, I think we have great conviction on. And as long as the market undervalues it's an opportunity from our perspective. But at the same time, our focus is on investing organically.

And if necessary, making other investments in the business to drive our growth in those core end markets that we're confident in.

Operator: Your next question comes from the line of Matt Akers with BNP Paribas.

Matthew (Matt) Akers: Most of mine have been answered. I just wanted to follow up on NASA. And just curious how much of your business remain that's with NASA? And just how are your discussions going with that customer in terms of do they want to start to grow the remaining portion of your business, or just kind of the general outlook for that customer?

Stephen Arnette: Yes. As we actually covered in the prepared remarks, NASA has moved to speed on executing the plan. And so they're really essentially complete with all of their insourcing actions, so that happened pretty quickly. Our remaining NASA business today know that our head count has stabilized, still is at a run rate of about $1 billion annually. So all that is good. And then to the second part of your question, we do and are already positioning for future opportunities with the agency. The fact remains we've established a many-decade partnership and based on the basis of successful engineering and scientific support to their missions. We are excited about specific growth opportunities that are in the future for us.

And so this year will be a reset to the lower revenue level. But beyond that, we think we'll begin to regrow from that baseline.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. This concludes today's call. You may now disconnect.

#3011. Pixel Weather’s new feature lets you report your local conditions now

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Tech > Services & Software > Operating Systems > Mobile OS > Android

Weather apps are notoriously inaccurate. Google's new feature can help.

Default weather apps are notoriously unreliable, but Google is giving users a chance to help improve things.

A recent update to the Pixel Weather app introduced a new “Report current weather” card. If the weather you’re experiencing doesn’t match what the app is saying, you can report the discrepancy.

“Share the current weather condition,” the card says, “to improve local forecasts.” If you tap it, you’re given options to indicate whether the current temperature is accurate, warmer, or colder than the app says, and what your current conditions are, with options like cloudy, clear, rain showers, strong thunderstorms, and rain showers.

The card also shows what the app currently thinks is happening for you to use as the basis for your report. To find the card, scroll all the way to the bottom of your Pixel Weather app.

Also: Your best Google weather app alternatives (and what I recommend instead)

Google said that it will use your feedback, device location, and “some diagnostic information” to help improve forecasts. Nothing you report will be associated with your Google account. The app doesn’t explain exactly how Google uses your reports, but I’ve reached out to see if the company can offer any details.

As someone who doesn’t put a ton of faith into default weather apps, I see this as a step in the right direction toward regaining some trust. Even if it’s not yet clear how Google will use the information you send, the goal of improving forecasts is an important one.

Also: I switched to MyRadar as my main Android Auto weather app and don’t regret it

A large part of what makes weather apps unreliable is that they lack human insight, and a computer usually can’t grasp the nuance of a local forecast the way a meteorologist would. Experts have also warned of reduced weather forecast accuracy due to recent NOAA budget cuts.

The Apple Weather app has a similar feature, so it’s good to see Google catch up. I couldn’t find a feature like this for Samsung or any other native app. One of the most popular third-party apps, Weather Underground, does feature a “Report your local weather” prompt. It also gathers information from hundreds of thousands of connected home weather stations.

This new Pixel Weather feature was present on three Pixel phones in my home, so the rollout appears to be widespread.

#3010. Google Imagines a Personalized TV Channel Full of AI Slop, Starring You

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

Google's rejected patent application was for a TV service that made videos based on your viewing habits.

If you’ve ever dreamed of starring in your own TV show, this might be for you. Google’s latest patent application is for an AI-powered version of your personalized TV channel, using data advertisers have gathered about you. The AI-created shows can also insert you as the main character.

According to the website Patentlyze, the application is for a system designed to compile your video or TV watch preferences using genres and titles you watch on services such as YouTube, plus context from your IP address and demographic data such as your age. Although Patentlyze says this particular Google patent application was rejected, the company can amend the application and resubmit.

A Google representative didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The system would include an option to make you the hero by building an avatar from your photos and replicating your voice for the lead character’s lines.

The program could create a personalized feed like “John’s Channel,” stocked with AI-made crime-comedy capers, rom-coms and sci-fi adventures, if those are the shows John enjoys. The service could make new videos based on voice prompts or create new ones on its own, the report said.

Building a channel of AI slop isn’t a new idea. Roku recently unveiled FairgroundTV, the first free, all-AI streaming channel.

Generative AI continues to draw widespread skepticism from both local communities and everyday internet users. New data centers built to power AI models have met growing grassroots resistance over their heavy energy and water footprints, while synthetic content faces mounting cultural pushback, especially from younger audiences, who have largely rejected AI-generated media as inauthentic “slop.”

#3008. Apple Reportedly Adding Product Red Options to HomePod Mini 2 and AirPods Max 2

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

It's been eight years since the two collaborated on the Apple iPhone 8.

If you’ve been waiting for an excuse to upgrade your home audio while supporting a good cause, here’s your chance. Apple is planning to revive its Product Red charity partnership with new versions of the HomePod Mini 2 and AirPods Max 2, according to a Bloomberg report. The $149 HomePod Mini 2 came out in early November and will now be offered with a red mesh cover as part of this collaboration. The AirPods Max 2 will come in silver, instead of red, but will feature a red digital crown.

While Apple has released red phone cases in the meantime, the last hardware collaboration came in 2018, when the iPhone 8 and 8 Plus were released in Product Red colors. Red cases were also released.

A representative for Apple didn’t immediately respond to a request for comment.

The release would coincide with the 20th anniversary of the first Product Red collaboration, the iPod Nano Red Special Edition. For that event, Apple contributed $10 from the sale of each device to the Global Fund to help fight HIV/AIDS in Africa. Product Red was founded in 2006 by politician Bobby Shriver and Bono of the band U2, and the iPod Nano Red special edition included music from U2.

Apple has yet to announce pricing and availability for the two devices. But according to the report, the product could be available Dec. 1, which is designated as World AIDS Day.

#3007. BingEx (FLX) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

Revenue slipped as delivery rivals intensified, but AI now handles 90% of service cases.

By Motley Fool Transcribing – Nov 24, 2026 at 2:57PM EST

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

BingEx (FLX -1.99%) reported a year-over-year decline in total revenue as competition in the Chinese on-demand delivery market intensified. Management maintained a stable gross margin through optimized merchant acquisition and disciplined spending while significantly expanding the role of artificial intelligence across research and operational functions. The company launched a new service category for everyday assistance and deepened integrations with major platform ecosystems to diversify user acquisition channels. Strategic focus remained on high-value delivery segments and improving the fulfillment capacity of the courier network while executing a multi-million dollar share repurchase program.

Operator: Good day, and welcome to BingEx' 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results Conference Call. Today's conference is being recorded. At this time, I would like to turn the conference over to Helen Wu from Piacente Financial Communications. Please go ahead.

Helen Wu: Thank you, operator. During this call, we will discuss our business outlook and make forward-looking statements. These comments are based on our predictions and expectations as of today. Actual events or results could differ materially from those mentioned in today's news release and in this discussion due to a number of risks and uncertainties, including those mentioned in our most recent filings with the SEC. The non-GAAP financial measures we provide are for comparison purpose only. The definition of these measures and a reconciliation table are available in the news release we issued earlier today. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

In addition, a webcast replay of this conference call will be available on the BingEx company's IR website at ir.ishansong.com. Furthermore, throughout the call, we will constantly use the company brand name FlashEx to refer to its publicly listed entity, BingEx Limited. Joining us today from FlashEx senior management are Mr. Adam Xue, Founder, Chairman of the Board and Chief Executive Officer; Mr. Hongjian Yu, Co-Founder, Director and Executive President; and Mr. Luke Tang, Chief Financial Officer. I will now turn the call over to Mr. Adam Xue.

Peng (Adam) Xue: Thank you, Helen. Hello, everyone, and welcome to FlashEx's Third Quarter 2026 Earnings Call. Competition in the on-demand delivery industry remained intense in the third quarter, responded by sharpening our execution and strengthening our differentiated on-demand dedicated courier model. We improved user acquisition efficiency, our merchant mix and fulfillment experience while also expanding into new scenarios and new cities at a measured pace. Doing this work well is what positions FlashEx for long-term growth. Let me start with our overall operations. We fulfilled 62.8 million orders in the third quarter, largely in line with the second quarter and average delivery time held steady at around 25.3 minutes.

As of the end of the third quarter, our registered users increased to 128 million, registered Flash Riders rose to 3.33 million and our service network expanded to 301 cities. As we keep growing our user base and delivery capacity, we are focusing more on turning these resources into reliable service capabilities while steadily improving operating efficiency. Turning to our financial performance. Total revenues for the third quarter were RMB 929.4 million with a gross margin of 11.2%. Non-GAAP income from operations was RMB 16.1 million. As of the end of the third quarter, our cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaled RMB 816.4 million, reflecting a healthy financial position.

We also remained committed to enhancing shareholder returns through share repurchases. As of November 23, we had repurchased a total of approximately 4.9 million ADS for an aggregate consideration of approximately USD 13.3 million. Now let me walk through our business in more detail. On the individual user side, we prioritize acquisition efficiency and the conversion of new users. We concentrated our marketing spend on higher converting channels in the third quarter, lowering new user acquisition cost by more than 30% quarter-over-quarter. First order conversion and order volume from new users both increased. Beyond our own channels, we are also reaching users by integrating our services into the ecosystem of major platforms.

Orders through our Quick Apps in the Huawei HarmonyOS ecosystem grew 27% quarter-over-quarter. Our partnership with Alipay expanded from assisted purchasing to its lifestyle services channel and users have begun placing orders through the Zhixiaobao AI agent. In terms of use cases, both our core categories and our diverse everyday lifestyle scenarios continued to grow. In cakes, a long-standing core category for us, order volume increased 19% year-over-year in the third quarter. This growth was driven by stronger gifting demand and stable partnerships with leading cake brands, reflecting the trust FlashEx has built with high-quality merchants over the years.

On the everyday side, total order volume across our 5 lifestyle scenarios grew 3.5% quarter-over-quarter, led by food pickup and parcel pickup. These everyday needs also point us in a clear direction for expanding our lifestyle services. With this in mind, we launched our new service, Flash Helper or Flash Assist in the third quarter. It brings the standardized processes and attentive one-on-one service to everyday needs such as waiting in line at restaurants, handling small tasks and moving or carrying items for users. Demand for this kind of assistance has long existed but remains highly fragmented.

Early results show that new users account for high share of Flash Helper orders, making the service an additional channel for expanding our user base and extending user lifetime. We will keep refining the service and use our existing Flash Rider network to explore more services that fit users' daily needs. For users with higher service expectations, we continue to refine our premium delivery service in the third quarter. Premium delivery order volume grew significantly quarter-over-quarter, and the number of new users increased by approximately 37%. This service further diversifies our product tiers, so we can better meet users' varying needs for speed and attention to detail.

On the merchant side, we focused on improving both the quality of our merchant base and our service capabilities while deepening our relationships with existing merchants. We concentrated on raising the quality of newly acquired merchants. To that end, we ran a pilot in 6 cities in northern China, where we optimized resource allocation based on merchants' operating profiles and flexibly adjusted pricing strategies to market conditions in each channel and city, balancing merchant acquisition with ongoing operations. These adjustments are already paying off with gross profit improving in the pilot cities. For our KA business, we moved into a tiered operating model, managing national and regional accounts separately, leveraging the stable high-density order flow from our enterprise clients channels.

We have built a strong delivery competitive base in core business districts, which in turn is driving new merchant acquisition and revenue growth in these areas. In the third quarter, average daily order volume from KA merchants grew quarter-over-quarter, and their share of GMV rose to 17.6%. As the quality of merchant business continues to improve, our business has become even more resilient. For entering new cities and new districts, we adopted a more return-driven expansion model. Our existing teams and our partners run this market directly, drawing on the people and experience we already have to get started quickly with lower upfront investment.

In the third quarter, average daily order volume in newly launched cities and districts rose sharply from the second quarter with some areas turning profitable within a short period. These results provide a proven template for future expansion. Going forward, we will replicate the model progressively, tailoring our approach to local market conditions as we enter new cities. Whether we are serving existing users or developing new services, reliable fulfillment always comes first. In the third quarter, we strengthened our delivery capacity by starting with the Flash Rider experience. We refined our tiered growth framework for Flash Riders with development paths for those riding regularly, those riding flexibly and those building advanced skills.

We also introduced an owner certification that recognizes Flash Riders for strong service and encourage them to keep improving. As Flash Rider income rose steadily, we saw a higher share of regular active Flash Riders and better fulfillment quality with the perfect order rate climbing further and the complaints continue to fall. Order completion rates also improved year-over-year during peak demand periods and in high-density areas such as holidays and core business districts. A stable, well-supported Flash Rider team ultimately translates into a more reliable experience for our users. Yesterday, we celebrated our ninth annual Flash Rider Day together with Flash Riders across the country.

Since we established the day in 2018, we have marked every November 3 by recognizing those who stand out for their professional service and good deeds in the community and by thanking all of our Flash Riders through online and offline events and benefits. Going forward, we will keep investing in safety, skills training, career development and everyday support, creating a better working environment and giving our Flash Riders more room to grow. Our Flash Riders' experience on the road are also helping more users understand the value of FlashEx.

In the third quarter, we built content around real-life Flash Rider stories and expanded our network of around 690 Flash Rider KOLs beyond Beijing to more cities using AI tools to produce and review content more efficiently. For the first time, we also combined a celebrity partnership, holiday timing and a new service in a single campaign, promoting Flash Helper's everyday assistance services during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. Our brand communications focus on showing users what FlashEx can do for them in specific real-life situations so that every service experience gradually adds up to trust in our brand.

On the technology front, we continued to put AI into practice to improve efficiency across R&D, customer service and operations. Efficiency gains in these areas increased from 30% in the second quarter to 46% in the third quarter. In R&D, the share of AI-assisted coding exceeded 98%. At the end of September, Super Agent, our self-developed internal development agent, completed its first development tasks end-to-end on its own. Next, we will extend AI further into requirement analysis, testing and release with the goal of shortening development cycles. In customer service, AI has moved beyond standardized Q&A into more open-ended inquiries, now handling close to 90% of cases in core scenarios allow our human agents to concentrate on more complex requests.

In operations, AI tools are increasingly used by our frontline teams. They are gradually moving into a more efficient digital way of working at every level from headquarters to the frontline. Our low-altitude delivery business moved into routine operations in the third quarter. By the end of the quarter, we have built 15 takeoff and landing sites and 24 2-way delivery routes in Hangzhou, covering the city's main districts. Order volume grew 13% quarter-over-quarter. Next, we will focus on 3 areas to further extend the service coverage and capabilities, building a denser network coordinating across channels and partnering with government and other enterprises. Looking ahead, we will focus on improving new users conversion and optimizing our merchant mix.

Building on our existing capabilities, we will also steadily expand our service scenarios and city network. We will also continue to invest in enhancing the experience of both our Flash Riders and our users and deepen the application of AI across our business to deliver better service with greater efficiency. For 12 years, FlashEx has built its business around on-demand dedicated courier services. Our focus has always been the same, providing reliable service the user needed at urgent and important moments. Going forward, with every high-quality delivery and service, we will keep building the trust that the users and merchants place in FlashEx and make that trust the foundation of a long-term sustainable growth. That concludes my remarks.

Now I will turn the call over to our CFO, Luke Tang. Thank you.

Le (Luke) Tang: Thank you, Adam. Hello, everyone. This is Luke. I would like now to walk you through our third quarter 2026 financial results. During the third quarter, our unique on-demand dedicated courier model remained resilient in a competitive market with order volume holding steady quarter-over-quarter. Backed by a disciplined approach to spending and a healthy cash position, we have the flexibility to keep investing in fulfillment quality while exploring new services and use cases. We also remain committed to enhancing shareholder returns through our repurchase program. Before I begin, please note that all numbers are in renminbi and all percentage changes are on year-over-year basis, unless otherwise noted.

Our revenues for the third quarter were RMB 929.4 million compared with RMB 1,005.4 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily driven by intensifying market competition. Our cost of revenues for the third quarter was RMB 824.8 million compared with RMB 893.6 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was in line with the decline in revenues. Our gross profit was RMB 104.5 million for the third quarter compared with RMB 111.8 million in the same period of 2025, representing a gross profit margin of 11.2% compared with 11.1% in the same period of 2025. Turning to operating expenses.

Our total operating expenses for the third quarter were RMB 93.5 million, representing a decrease of 4.3% from RMB 97.7 million in the same period of 2025. They consisted of RMB 40.3 million in selling and marketing expenses, RMB 36.6 million in general and administrative expenses and RMB 16.6 million in research and development expenses. The decrease in operating expenses was mainly attributable to the reduction in advertising expenses and share-based compensation expenses. Our income from operations was RMB 11.1 million compared with RMB 14.1 million in the same period of 2025. Excluding share-based compensation expenses, our non-GAAP income from operations was RMB 16.1 million for the third quarter compared with RMB 23.7 million in the same period of 2025.

Our net loss was RMB 6.8 million compared with net income of RMB 43.7 million in the same period of 2025. The change was mainly due to an investment loss of RMB 19.7 million in the third quarter compared with investment income of RMB 33.2 million in the same period of 2025. Excluding changes in fair value of long-term investments and share-based compensation expenses, our non-GAAP net loss was RMB 1 million compared with non-GAAP net income of RMB 62.6 million in the same period of 2025. Our cash position remained healthy with cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments totaling RMB 816.4 million as of the third quarter end.

We also continue to carry out share repurchases under our existing buyback program. As of November 23, we had repurchased a total of approximately 4.9 million ADS in the open market for an aggregate consideration of approximately USD 13.3 million. This underscores our confidence in the company's long-term value. As we close out 2026, we remain committed to disciplined execution and to the high-quality service that differentiates us with a distinctive business model and an improving merchant mix and the deeper use of AI across our operations. We are confident in our ability to create sustainable long-term value for our shareholders. That concludes our prepared remarks. We would like to open the floor to your questions. Operator, please go ahead.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] We will now take our first question. This question comes from the line of [indiscernible] from CICC.

Unknown Analyst: This is [indiscernible] from CICC. Actually, two questions on my side. The first one is about margins and financials. We noticed that our gross margins held up well, yet operating margins compressed. Could you please walk us through what drove the pressures on the OpEx side? And on the non-GAAP net loss swing, how much of that is operating versus below the line items? And my second question is about shareholder returns. You still have about half of the buyback authorization remaining. How should we think about the pace of repurchase going forward, particularly given the current earnings trajectory?

Le (Luke) Tang: Thank you, [indiscernible]. I will take your first question and hand over the second one to Adam. Yes, our gross margin held steady this quarter. So the change in operating margin came mainly from operating expenses due to new initiatives we launched. During the third quarter, we launched Flash Helper, which helps users do everyday tasks such as waiting in line at restaurants or moving or carrying items. And we promoted it with our first celebrity campaign around the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holidays. So compared with the second quarter, we spent more on marketing to support these launches. We also kept investing in R&D, especially in AI.

We are already using AI tools to create and review marketing content faster. And over time, we expect them to make our marketing spend more efficient. Going forward, we will remain disciplined on overall spending. On a non-GAAP basis, there was a decrease in the fair value of our short-term investments in the third quarter. Our core business stayed profitable with a non-GAAP income from operations of RMB 16.1 million. Yes, I would like to hand over the second question to Adam.

Peng (Adam) Xue: Okay. Thank you, Luke. And also thank you, [indiscernible], for your question. I will answer the second question. Well, our commitment to creating value for shareholders hasn't changed, and that is what guides our buyback program. In terms of progress, as of November 23, we have bought back about 4.9 million ADS for around USD 13.3 million under our USD 30 million program. Buybacks are one of several ways we return value to shareholders. As for the pace from here, we will stay flexible, taking into account market conditions, operating performance and our funding needs and act when the time is right in compliance with applicable SEC rules. Our balance sheet gives us a solid base for this.

We ended the quarter with RMB 816.4 million in cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash and short-term investments. Over the long run, we believe that continuing to strengthen our business, combined with prudent use of share repurchases is the best way to create long-term shareholder value. The buyback program also reflects our confidence in the company's long-term prospects.

Operator: That concludes our Q&A session for today. I will now hand back to Helen Wu for closing remarks.

Helen Wu: Thank you once again for joining BingEx' Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Business Update Conference Call today. If you have any further questions, please contact the IR team at BingEx or Piacente Financial Communications. Thank you and have a great day.

Operator: Thank you. This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for participating. You may now disconnect.

#3006. You won’t see a Galaxy Watch 10 until 2028 – here’s why

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

In an effort to cut costs, Samsung is postponing the launch of the Galaxy Watch 10, according to reports. Here's what to know.

You might have to wait over a year to get the Samsung Galaxy Watch 10: Samsung will not release any new Galaxy smartwatch in 2027, South Korea’s ET News reported on Sunday.

In an effort to cut costs after two quarters of consecutive losses and amid global RAM shortages, Samsung Electronics’ Mobile Business division will switch from an annual release schedule to a biannual one for its smartwatches, according to ET News. The switch follows other cost-cutting measures that will reduce production of the tech giant’s midrange smartphone lineup while increasing its premium Galaxy S27 offerings.

I am not mad at this decision by Samsung. Annual smartwatch updates are usually iterative anyway. Take Apple, for example. Its Apple Watch Series 10, released in 2024, had the same chip as the Apple Watch Series 11, released a year later. The most recent Apple Watch, the Apple Watch Series 12, has the same battery life as the Apple Watch Series 11. I’d expect Apple to keep its new sensors, which debuted on the Series 12 and Ultra 4, for its Series 13 or Ultra 5 next year.

Samsung’s Galaxy Watch 9, which debuted with a different chip and added a few more hours of battery, had the same bones as the Galaxy Watch 8.

If some of the biggest features on these smartwatches remain the same for a few years, why not change the release schedule to a biannual one?

Also: Galaxy Watch 9 vs. Galaxy Watch 8: I’ve compared both models, here’s my advice

Some of the most substantial updates that arrive on new devices like the Galaxy Watch 9 or Apple Watch Series 12 normally arrive through software updates, which end up landing on previous watch generations upon launch as well.

By switching from an annual release cycle to a biannual one, Samsung could drum up more excitement and anticipation between launches, and be able to surprise its customers with more purchase-worthy updates.

Samsung did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

#3005. SpaceX Sued by 2 States Over Grok’s Sexualized Images of Women and Children

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

People used Grok to generate millions of "spicy mode" images.

Oregon and Virginia on Monday filed lawsuits against SpaceX, alleging that Elon Musk’s company violated consumer protection laws, months after people used Grok Imagine to generate millions of sexualized images of women and children.

Grok Imagine is an image- and video-generation tool developed by SpaceXSI, a division of SpaceX. Shortly after launching last summer, the tool added a “spicy mode,” which enabled people to generate images and videos showing partial nudity and adult-themed videos. Grok Imagine is integrated into Grok, which is Musk’s AI chatbot.

In the lawsuits, separate but jointly filed, Virginia and Oregon allege that the sexualized images — including child sexual abuse material — were generated without the knowledge and consent of the women and children shown in the images and videos.

Read more: After Rampant AI-Powered Abuse, Grok Doubles Down

Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in a press release that SpaceX misled people into thinking that their images and data would be safe.

“When xAI [now renamed SpaceXSI] allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritized growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it,” Jones said. “Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable.”

Donna Rice Hughes, CEO of child internet safety organization Enough Is Enough, praised Oregon and Virginia for taking action against SpaceX.

“It is abhorrent that women and children are preyed upon in this manner and even more repugnant that xAI’s Grok ‘spicy mode’ has not kept up with bad actors who abuse their terms of service,” Hughes told CNET, adding that Musk’s “team can find ways to prevent criminal misuse of Grok, and at the very least, disable Grok’s ‘spicy mode.'”

Grok Imagine launched on Aug. 5, 2025, and within months, it was used to generate millions of sexualized images, which were posted on the social media platform X, which is also owned by Musk’s SpaceX.

Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield alleged SpaceX “knowingly designed” Grok Imagine and promoted spicy mode’s lack of safeguards as a feature, not a bug.

“It’s no surprise that Grok and X became a haven for perpetrators using AI to create and share child sexual abuse material,” Rayfield said in a statement. “The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug, which they promoted as ‘spicy mode.’”

During a 9-day span starting in late December, Grok posted about 3 million sexualized images, according to an analysis from the Center for Countering Digital Hate.

In a statement posted Monday on X, SpaceX said that people using Grok to generate sexualized images and videos violated the platform’s terms of service and worked “aggressively to circumvent our safeguards.” The company said it tightened protections after the misuse and continues to test and adjust them as needed. SpaceX also said it notifies law enforcement authorities “when someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content.”

Earlier this year, several minor Jane Does filed a proposed class action lawsuit against xAI after people used their photos to generate child sexual abuse material using Grok via spicy mode. That case is still ongoing.

In July, a victim’s family also filed suit after photographer Russell Bloodworth in Arkansas allegedly used spicy mode to generate explicit photos of children. xAI went on the offensive, suing Bloodworth and South Carolina man Terry Wayne Harwood, who is also accused of using Grok to generate child sexual abuse material. The company seeks damages for expenses incurred in fighting lawsuits and for reputational harm.

SpaceX and xAI have faced lawsuits for other things aside from illicit image generation. The companies were sued for allegedly sharing sensitive data and for allegedly causing users to be hospitalized for psychosis after harmful chat conversations on Grok.

Monday’s lawsuits against SpaceX are among nearly 400 cases brought against 129 AI companies in the US, according to the AI Lawsuit Tracker. Many Big Tech companies have been sued for allegedly harming the mental health of adults and children. In August, Meta agreed to pay $18 billion to settle a lawsuit brought by US states alleging the company intentionally designed Instagram and other platforms to be addictive to children.

Companies such as ByteDance — owner of TikTok — Snap, Google and others face more than 2,400 federal lawsuits alleging that their platforms harm the mental health of children.

Wired headphones proved to be a real surprise category this year, and Sony recently cashed in by releasing the MDR-3R wired headphones, which proved so popular that they've sold out three times since launching mere weeks ago.

Good news for you, fans of the 80s: The Sony MDR-3R are back in stock, so you better act fast before they sell out again.

A post shared by Tom's Guide (@tomsguide)

The Sony MDR-3R headphones are currently only available in silver with orange and blue earpads (you get a set of each). The "Stranger Things" limited edition models are still sold out.

As iconic as the Sony Walkman, Sony's headphones were that era's AirPods; instantly recognizable by anyone who spotted them on the street. The 2026 version of these trades in the 3.5mm headphone jack for a USB-C port, which makes more sense given how many smartphones have ditched dedicated audio ports. It also has a set of inline volume controls as well as a microphone, so you can use them to take phone calls.

Now, don't expect stellar audio quality out of these, but our own Kate Kozuch took a pair for a spin, and said that they're definitely more for the look than the fidelity. This is a nostalgia play more than anything else.

As of this writing, Sony is estimating a ship date of December 5, so you'll have to wait a week or two before you get them. But, if you're planning on gifting them, it'll leave you plenty of time to get them wrapped.

#3003. Top Wall Street analysts are bullish on the growth potential of these 3 stocks

Fears around the artificial intelligence trade and higher pressure on oil prices are weighing on global markets, but a few stocks offer investors solid growth prospects even in choppy times.

Investors with a long-term horizon can look beyond the ongoing volatility and track the recommendations of top Wall Street analysts to pick attractive stocks with strong long-term growth potential.

Here are three stocks favored by some of Wall Street's top pros, according to TipRanks, a platform that ranks analysts based on their past performance.

Health insurer UnitedHealth delivered better-than-expected results for the third quarter of 2026. The company also raised its full-year earnings outlook, reflecting continued progress on its turnaround plan.

Following the Q3 print, Morgan Stanley analyst Erin Wright reiterated a buy rating on UNH stock with a price target of $529. "UNH's beat & raise reinforces turnaround momentum, with improving MA [Medicare Advantage]/Optum Health supporting a higher '26 EPS baseline & upside to '27 consensus," said Wright.

The five-star analyst added that better-than-expected performance in the UnitedHealthcare and Optum Health businesses supported another upgrade to the company's 2026 adjusted earnings per share outlook to at least $20.50. Wright noted that UNH raised the earnings guidance despite incremental investments planned for the fourth quarter of 2026.

Furthermore, Wright highlighted management's view that the consensus 2027 EPS of $22.63 was too conservative. Reaching even the low end of the company's 13% to 16% long-term EPS growth target would imply an EPS of $23.17.

Wright raised her 2026 EPS estimate to $20.65 from $19.82 and 2027 EPS to $23.24 from $22.54, reflecting the latest upside and an improving 2026 medical loss ratio to 87.4% from 88.1%. Overall, she believes that UNH's operational performance continues to improve, increasing her confidence in its UHC strategy and Optum Health turnaround execution.

Wright ranks No. 264 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. Her ratings have been successful 64% of the time, delivering an average return of 15%. See UnitedHealth Ownership Structure on TipRanks.

Social media giant Meta Platforms has been making headlines since the launch of its Muse AI agent, which is seeing solid traction. Investors look forward to updates on the company's AI strategy when it announces its third-quarter results on Oct. 21.

Heading into Q3 earnings, Guggenheim analyst Michael Morris maintained a buy rating on Meta stock and increased his price target to $850 from $700, reflecting higher estimates for 2027. He expects Muse usage momentum and engagement levels to shape investor sentiment into the Q3 earnings call.

Specifically, Morris highlighted that, according to Apptopia, Muse reached 1.3 million daily active users in five weeks versus 300,000 in the first week. Given that Muse's current adoption represents less than 0.05% of Meta's 3.6 billion daily active user base, the analyst expects management to prioritize boosting usage over near-term monetization.

"Over time, we believe Muse monetizes primarily through businesses paying to reach consumers through their agents, consistent with the economics of Meta's core advertising business, rather than consumer wallets," said the five-star analyst. He added that the checkout integrations with Shopify and PayPal reflect this framework.

While there are concerns that a rival could overtake Muse or the recently launched Muse Wonder and push Meta into a prolonged cycle of overinvestment, Morris remains bullish due to the company's strong record in scaling WhatsApp and competing strongly with TikTok via Reels as well as free distribution to an extensive user base.

Morris ranks No. 629 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been successful 57% of the time, delivering an average return of 13.2%. See Meta Platforms KPIs on TipRanks.

Next is semiconductor company Marvell Technology. Earlier this month, Marvell held its Investor Day, where it raised its total addressable market estimate to $400 billion by 2030, reflecting solid AI-led demand tailwinds.

After hosting a non-deal roadshow with Marvell's senior management following the Investor Day, Stifel analyst Tore Svanberg reiterated a buy rating on the stock with a price target of $370.

The five-star analyst said that a major focus of the roadshow was the XPU and XPU Attach mix, as Marvell's Custom business expands toward its FY31 revenue target of $30 billion. In this regard, management reiterated that it expects a balanced mix of XPU and XPU Attach revenue in FY31, though it noted that either segment could grow rapidly enough to shift the mix toward 60/40 or 40/60.

While XPU drove most of the nearly $1.5 billion Custom revenue in FY26, Svanberg expects Marvell's XPU Attach business to grow substantially through the end of the decade, leading to a more balanced mix in this business. At the Investor Day event, the company raised its FY29 Custom target from more than $10 billion to over $12 billion, mainly driven by strength in the XPU Attach business.

Svanberg said that another key topic in the roadshow was whether Marvell can secure enough capacity to meet its raised targets. Management said that it met with suppliers ahead of Investor Day to share its five-year goals and received commitments to support these targets. The analyst believes that Marvell's supply chain commitments give it a competitive edge over rivals as customers seek reliable partners for large-scale infrastructure buildouts.

Svanberg ranks No. 91 among more than 12,500 analysts tracked by TipRanks. His ratings have been profitable 58% of the time, delivering an average return of 31.8%. See Marvell Technology Statistics on TipRanks.

#3002. Axon Enterprise vs. Palantir Technologies: Which Law Enforcement Stock Is a Better Buy for 2027?

Axon's revenue jumped 33.6% while Palantir's surged 87.1%, but the valuation gap between the two is hard to ignore.

By Brendan Coffey – Updated Nov 24, 2026 at 3:00PM EST

10 stocks we like better than Axon Enterprise ›

Investors searching for exposure to mission-critical software and hardware often compare Axon Enterprise (AXON +3.81%) and Palantir Technologies (PLTR +1.14%). Both companies leverage sophisticated technology to solve complex problems for large institutions.

Axon specializes in public safety tools and cloud evidence management for law enforcement. Palantir provides massive data integration and artificial intelligence infrastructure for government and corporate clients. As both companies expand their digital platforms, determining which is the more attractive buy requires a look at their recent financial performance.

Axon Enterprise provides a comprehensive ecosystem of hardware and software designed for law enforcement and public safety professionals. Its product line includes Taser devices, body-worn cameras, and the Axon Evidence platform, which allows agencies to manage digital records securely. The company is actively expanding its presence among defense stocks and international markets across Europe and Asia. No single customer represented more than 10% of total net sales in 2025, which provides a diversified revenue base.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $3.4 billion, indicating a 33.6% increase compared to the prior period. This growth was accompanied by a net income of approximately $258.5 million. The company continues to transition customers toward subscription-based software services, which typically offer higher visibility into future sales. This steady growth suggests strong demand for its integrated safety solutions among federal and local agencies.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is roughly 0.6x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholder equity, showing how much the company relies on borrowed funds. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, is approximately 2.5x. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow was around $75.1 million. Note that stock-based compensation represented roughly 300% of operating cash flow, meaning reported cash generation is heavily inflated by this non-cash add-back.

Palantir Technologies develops platforms that integrate and analyze massive data sets to help organizations make better decisions. Its customer base is divided between government agencies and commercial enterprises, with a total of 954 customers as of late 2025. The company recently reported a remaining deal value of nearly $11.2 billion, split between its public and private sector contracts. Note that the top three customers accounted for roughly 16% of revenue in 2025. Customer concentration among these top clients adds a layer of risk to the business.

In the 12 months ended Sept. 30, 2026, revenue reached about $7.3 billion, representing a significant 87% increase over the previous 12 months. Net income for this period was approximately $3.7 billion. This surge in performance is driven by the rapid adoption of its artificial intelligence infrastructure. The company often uses low-cost pilot deployments to prove the value of its software before moving to larger, long-term contracts.

As of its December 2025 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.0x, showing the company has no debt relative to its equity. The current ratio is roughly 7.1x, indicating a strong ability to cover short-term financial obligations with existing assets. In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, free cash flow reached nearly $2.1 billion. Note that stock-based compensation (SBC) accounted for roughly 32% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back in the cash flow statement.

Axon Enterprise faces risks related to the acceptance of its products by law enforcement agencies. Negative publicity regarding its devices or software can impact demand. The company also faces global supply chain dependencies and rapid technological shifts, particularly in artificial intelligence. Legal risks include product liability claims and complex government procurement regulations. It competes in an environment alongside companies such as Motorola Solutions (MSI +0.04%).

Palantir Technologies carries risks associated with its revenue concentration, as a small number of customers provide a large portion of its total sales. The company also manages long and unpredictable sales cycles that require significant upfront investment. There is a risk that its AI technologies may fail to gain further market acceptance. Additionally, the company relies heavily on third-party cloud infrastructure from providers like Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN -1.21%) and Microsoft Corp. (MSFT +0.74%).

Palantir Technologies carries a notably higher valuation than Axon Enterprise when comparing both future earnings estimates and sales over the past twelve months.

Valuation metrics include those sourced from Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) and may differ from those of other data providers.

Axon has a positive long-term outlook for growth as law enforcement is increasingly equipped with Tasers and the public is becoming increasingly demanding that agents wear body cameras. Its cloud-based evidence control system is also an increasingly sought-after service for law enforcement organization.

Expansion into Europe and Canada should also help, as should a focus on producing personal consumer-protection devices. In particular, all the data and video created by Axon customers have to be managed, and the company is seeing strong demand for its AI-based management systems from customers who find many of the services create efficiencies within their operations.

In fiscal 2026, sales are expected to grow well, up about a third to $3.6 billion, with net income of around $290 million and free cash flow of $425 million, well over 2025's levels. In 2027, consensus estimates project adding another $1 billion in revenue, with expanding net income and free cash flow as well.

Palantir started out as a tech contractor to the U.S. military and law enforcement, and the federal government still accounts for half of its revenue. But the business has been successfully expanding beyond government work, with about a quarter of sales coming from international customers and a significant minority of revenue from the private sector. For the first time last quarter, private sector revenue exceeded U.S. government revenue.

Palantir says customers are drawn to its sovereign AI, which is its term for systems that can help build themselves while protecting what makes each system the AI is refining, so it is not commoditized. Companies like Nvidia Corp. (NVDA -5.86%) and L3Harris Technologies (LHX +1.27%) are notable customers of Palantir's sovereign AI.

The boom in private-sector AI business should double Palantir's 2026 sales to $8.6 billion, with a $2.7 billion jump in net income to $4.4 billion. 2027 should see continued fast growth, with consensus analysts' estimates projecting revenue of $13.1 billion and net income over $6 billion.

The top-line growth of Palantir is difficult to ignore, but its shares trade at an exceptional premium that may not account for the long-term threat of AI displacing its business. Axon comes at a premium, too, as seen through its P/E and P/S ratios, but it's cheaper than Palantir, and the company is delivering exceptional sales growth and improving margins. For 2027, go with Axon Enterprise.

#3000. Uber Riders Can Now Request to Have Their Trips Recorded

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Our expert, award-winning staff selects the products we cover and rigorously researches and tests our top picks. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission.

In four cities, Uber riders can request rides with drivers who use the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in select markets will be able to specify that they want their trip recorded on video. The feature, which is being introduced in Baltimore, Indianapolis, St. Louis, and Raleigh, North Carolina, adds a new Recorded Rides choice to the app alongside other familiar ride options like UberX and UberXL. Uber says that the new feature gives “greater confidence that a recording will be there if something doesn’t go as planned.”

After a series of rider safety investigations and sexual assault lawsuit settlements, Uber began looking for ways to boost passenger safety and confidence in the service. The ridesharing platform first tested in-app trip audio recording in late 2019, then piloted the Record My Ride feature in 2022, before finally rolling out the video recording function in earnest, first in San Francisco in 2023, then nationally across the US in 2024.

According to Uber, the knowledge that a trip is being recorded gives both riders and drivers peace of mind.

While drivers can opt out of using the feature in their settings, more than half of its active drivers in the US choose to record their trips in the Record My Ride feature.

Starting this week, Uber riders in those four cities will be able to request a recorded ride during the hailing process in the Uber app and, when possible, be automatically matched with a driver using the feature. Choosing a recorded ride doesn’t affect the fare.

Record My Ride has been available to Uber’s drivers, though not passengers, for a few years now. The feature uses the front-facing camera on the driver’s phone to capture trip audio and video.

“Uber can only review recordings uploaded as part of a safety report or insurance claim,” a representative told CNET.

Not selecting a Recorded Ride doesn’t guarantee that your trip won’t be recorded in some way. Many Uber drivers choose to install separate dash cams in their vehicles, often with multiple cameras recording into the cabin. Uber offers drivers the option to register their dash cam with the service, but this is separate from the pilot.

“Drivers can use a separate dash cam, provided they comply with local laws,” an Uber representative told CNET in an email, “but Recorded Rides specifically matches riders with drivers recording through Record My Ride.”

Uber says it’s exploring additional ways to use recordings to keep its riders and drivers safe. It will soon begin proactively activating the Record My Ride feature on drivers’ devices during trips that may benefit from additional oversight, such as late-night or trips involving teenagers. Uber is also looking into automatically turning on video recordings “when trips are not proceeding as expected,” such as when a trip goes significantly off the projected course or if a crash is detected.

Uber says it’s also looking into testing the automatic activation of audio recording on riders’ phones during nighttime trips. Passengers would have to consent to this, which would require the app to use their phone’s microphone.

#2999. Claude can ship code for you now – how to try it (if you dare)

Our gifting experts are obsessively searching for holiday gifts that are unique, thoughtful and suitable for any budget.

Would you let a few Claude agents review and ship your code for you?

Developers are already using Claude Code and other AI-powered coding tools like OpenAI’s Codex in droves, but some still want to check code themselves before pushing it. A new feature from Anthropic is banking on more adventurous, agent-first coders being comfortable with handing even that last step off to AI.

With Claude Ship, announced in beta Monday, “Claude can now review pull requests, fix them, and approve the ones that a team’s policy allows,” Anthropic said. The feature is geared toward individual developers or companies who want to move faster or already delegate a significant amount of coding tasks to agents.

Also: How I made a paid Mac app in 11 days with Claude – without writing a single line of code

“Teams stay in control of where it runs and which changes need a person,” Anthropic said. “The goal: ship code as fast as teams write it.”

The new feature uses two new agents alongside Code Review, which Anthropic released in March for Teams and Enterprise plans. Code Review first collects, organizes, and posts findings to a PR. Then, Anthropic said, the agents, PR Steward and Claude Approvals, guide a PR “through review, fixes, and an approval decision so teams don’t have to manage each step manually.”

PR Steward can’t approve or merge pull requests, designed instead to participate “on failing CI checks, merge conflicts, and review feedback from Code Review, other review tools, or team members.” It also documents what it changed in each push through comments and provides instructions for how to undo it, should developers want to. Throughout the process, developers can give Claude instructions or tell it to stop by commenting @claude.

Also: I tried replacing Claude Code with a local AI stack that’s completely free – how it went

As a final step, Claude Approvals references whatever policy the user or team abides by (which developers provide as a repo file), and additional signals developers set, like Code Review findings, before approving changes autonomously if allowed. If not, it will seek out “deeper human sign-off,” Anthropic said.

“It works like a smarter CODEOWNERS file,” the release added. Anthropic said it recommends that most customers enable those additional checks “first in observe-only mode to build confidence before configuring branch protection to require Claude Approvals’ green light.”

Admins can select which repos the feature runs in and adjust settings as needed.

But Claude Ship isn’t meant for everyone.

“Most teams want a person to approve every change, and that’s easy to keep up with when people write every line. But a lot of developers build with agents now,” Anthropic said in the release, noting that its own Claude Code team uses Claude to write a majority of the code it needs.

ZDNET senior contributing editor David Gewirtz said the idea of shipping code at the speed of writing it “raises the hair on the back of my neck.” But he added that, given how impressive Claude Code has been thus far, he wouldn’t be surprised if Anthropic’s deployment tools were equally effective.

Also: Claude Code vs. Codex: Why I use both and how to choose one (if you must)

“But, it does depend on the team’s workflow and the kind of development they’re doing,” he said. “It’s not something for every team and certainly not for every indy developer, but for certain deployment processes, it could shave a ton of time off turnaround, saving money and potentially sending fixes to customers much faster. ‘Tis cool.”

Ultimately, Gewirtz said he has reasons to both trust the tool and be concerned about what it means for younger developers in the workplace.

“Since that workflow is often assigned to less experienced members of the team, it’s likely that Claude would be as accurate, although it’s one more way to shut the junior members out of where they add value to the company and grow their skills to become senior decision makers,” he said.

Developer platforms overall are adapting to the new state of the industry. Entire, a GitHub competitor started by the Microsoft-owned platform’s former CEO, is built around the expectation that developers are working side-by-side with agents.

Individuals with a Pro, Max, or Ultra subscription can use the /ship command now available in Claude Code, meaning “users won’t notice any significant increase in token usage,” an Anthropic representative explained. Team and Enterprise users can use Claude Ship for Github repos, and it is billed on tokens, so your overall bill may change.

Still, that depends on the number of PRs users are putting through Claude Ship — to avoid any surprises, admins can set spending limits for both Code Review and the new PR Steward agent. They can also turn Claude Ship on for an entire repo, meaning developers won’t need the /ship command.

Anthropic added that certain Enterprise organizations “can claim at least $10,000 in Claude Ship credits to use within 30 days of claiming” by Jan. 15, 2027.

Also: How I safely run my OpenClaw AI agent 24/7 on a Mac – with Claude Code standing guard
